title: Prompt Injection
desc: Manipulation of LLM behavior through crafted inputs that override system-level instructions. Attack surface extends to any content the model parses — not just text input fields.
subtypes: Direct PI — user input explicitly overrides system prompt
Indirect PI — adversarial content in RAG/documents/search results
Multi-turn PI — injection spread across conversation turns
Cross-context PI — propagates between agents
Purchased PI Template — pre-optimized jailbreak from underground market
surface: Text input, RAG pipeline, document ingestion, API messages field, tool outputs
update: v1.5: Standard per-event detectors fail against slow-burn multi-turn attacks. Temporal accumulation detection required.

title: Excessive Agency
wild: 4/5 — EchoLeak, Copilot CRM leak confirmed in production
desc: LLM granted more tool/action permissions than necessary. Force multiplier for prompt injection: without agency, PI manipulates outputs; with agency, PI becomes remote code execution equivalent.
subtypes: Unbounded tool access — model calls any registered tool without confirmation
Privilege escalation via PI
Chained tool use — multi-step chain without human review
Cross-system action — email, file write, payment outside AI boundary
surface: Tool registration, function calling API, MCP servers

title: Supply Chain Compromise
wild: 4/5 — JFrog/ReversingLabs confirmed malicious models on HuggingFace
desc: Malicious or backdoored models, adapters, dependencies, MCP servers, or skills from third parties. Attack is entirely silent — no behavioral deviation during normal operation.
subtypes: Malicious model on public registry
Backdoored LoRA/PEFT adapter
Compromised MCP server or skill package
Poisoned dependency (pip/npm)
surface: Model registry, adapter repository, dependency install, MCP marketplace

title: Data / Model Poisoning
desc: Compromising training data, fine-tuning datasets, or RAG document stores to influence model behavior at a systemic level.
subtypes: Training data poisoning — corrupted data influences model weights
Fine-tuning dataset poisoning
RAG context poisoning — injecting adversarial documents at index time
Feedback loop poisoning — RLHF reward hacking via manipulated ratings
surface: Training pipeline, fine-tuning datasets, RAG document stores, feedback/rating systems

title: System Prompt Leakage
wild: 3/5 — Extraction techniques documented; iterative prompting required
desc: Extraction of system prompts, API keys, or proprietary instructions through iterative prompting or context manipulation.
subtypes: Direct extraction — asking the model to repeat its system prompt
Indirect extraction — inferring instructions from model behavior
API key/secret leakage embedded in system prompt
surface: System prompt, developer message, any context containing secrets

title: Model Extraction
desc: Query-based replication of proprietary models. Low risk for general-purpose LLMs; elevated for specialized or fine-tuned models with significant IP.
subtypes: Black-box extraction via crafted query sequences
Distillation from API outputs
surface: Public API endpoints with high query volume access

title: Embedding / Vector Weaknesses
wild: 2/5 — Specialized techniques; requires large query volume
desc: Reconstructing sensitive information from embedding vectors, or leaking data through query-pattern side channels in vector stores.
subtypes: Embedding inversion — reconstructing training data from embedding vectors
Cross-tenant vector store leakage
Query-pattern side channel — inferring other users' data from search patterns
surface: Embedding APIs, vector stores/databases, similarity search endpoints

title: Denial of Service / Unbounded Consumption
desc: Context/quota exhaustion degrading LLM service availability. Enterprise metered APIs can be financially destructive — attacker pays nothing, victim loses service AND pays for the calls.
subtypes: Context window exhaustion — max-length inputs
API quota exhaustion — standard API (score 12)
Enterprise metered API exhaustion — $10K+/month budgets (score 16)
Rate limit abuse
surface: Any LLM API endpoint; metered enterprise deployments especially

title: Multi-Agent Context Propagation
wild: 3/5 — Source-confirmed data-flow risk; exploitation depends on deployment
desc: PI propagates between chained agents, amplifying impact. Each agent hop can escalate privilege. Common in enterprise RAG and agentic assistant deployments.
subtypes: Output-to-input propagation
Privilege escalation across agent chain
MCP / A2A protocol injection
Agent-to-agent trust exploitation
surface: Multi-agent pipelines, MCP servers, A2A communication, LangChain/AutoGen deployments

title: Non-Text Injection
desc: Image, audio, or structured data injection bypassing text-focused input filters. Impact 4 because it circumvents most standard detection.
subtypes: Image-embedded PI (vision models)
Audio injection via ASR pipeline
Structured data (JSON/XML/CSV) injection
PDF/document visual injection
surface: Multi-modal endpoints, vision models, ASR pipelines, document ingestion

title: Output Validation Failures
wild: 3/5 — Standard in LLM deployments without output validation
desc: Harmful or unsafe model output passes to users or downstream systems unchecked. Especially critical when output is executed (code generation, instructions, structured data fed to other systems).
subtypes: Harmful content generation passed to user
Generated code execution without safety check
Structured output (JSON/SQL) used directly in downstream systems
Hallucinated facts presented as authoritative
surface: Any LLM output path; critical for code generation, instruction generation, structured output

title: HITL Failures
desc: Human reviewers fail to catch adversarial manipulation because context provenance is missing. Reviewers cannot distinguish legitimate outputs from PI-influenced outputs without provenance.
subtypes: Missing provenance — reviewer sees output without source context
Review fatigue — high volume reduces scrutiny
Sophistication gap — reviewer lacks ML security expertise
Time pressure override — SLA pressure defeats safety review
surface: Any HITL checkpoint; approval workflows; human review queues

title: Defense Control Type Confusion
desc: Alignment controls (model instructions) are mistaken for infrastructure-enforced controls. Most common security mistake in LLM deployments — creates false confidence in defenses that fail under attack.
subtypes: Treating system prompt instructions as hard security boundaries
Using alignment-only controls for compliance requirements
Assuming model refusals are reliable under adversarial conditions
surface: Architectural design phase; security review; compliance mapping
update: Addendum: Capability Withholding is a taxonomic note — accidental RLHF reward hacking is an operational concern, not a documented external attack path.

title: Internal Safety Collapse / Validator Harness Attack
wild: 5/5 for research pattern — ISC-Bench: 53 scenarios, 95.3% worst-case failure
desc: A benign-looking task + format validator + incomplete data harness causes harmful generation as the only valid task completion. Standard PI detectors miss it entirely — no injection present; harmful content IS the task-correct output.
subtypes: Task/Validator/Data (TVD) harness attack
Coding harness with harmful completion required
Data-labeling or eval harness manipulation
Fine-tuning dataset construction as attack vector
Autonomous workflow bundle injection
surface: Any system where attacker can shape task + validator + data: coding assistants, eval frameworks, data-labeling tools, fine-tuning pipelines, autonomous agents
update: arXiv:2603.23509 — ISC-Bench primary research; 8 disciplines; provider-side AND deployer-side controls both required.
